skill.name: linear-issues-read
skill.description: Read Linear issue data through documented Bun CLI commands using a Linear API key.
skill.summary: Read and filter Linear issues from a local CLI.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: Most command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code spans, not executable Ruby backtick evaluation. The confirmed issues are credential handling risks: the skill declares and documents LINEAR_API_KEY access and tells users to place it in a project .env file. No prompt injection, covert exfiltration instructions, or malicious business logic were found in the two scanned files.

remediation.suggestion: Request a least-privilege Linear API key, document required read scopes, and avoid printing environment values.
Prefer scoped secret storage or exported environment variables. If .env is supported, warn users to keep it out of version control.
Ship the referenced scripts with the package and advise users to inspect them before running Bun commands.

content.user_title: Review Linear Issues from the CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need quick access to Linear issue details without opening the web app. This skill documents read-only CLI commands for listing and viewing issues.
actual_capabilities: Documents a list-issues command with team, project, assignee, status, limit, and JSON options.
Documents a get-issue command for Linear issue identifiers and UUIDs.
Declares LINEAR_API_KEY as the required authentication secret.
Lists the Bun runtime and @linear/sdk dependency requirements.
Defines terminal output behavior for table and JSON results.
limitations: The scanned package contains only SKILL.md and skill.json, so implementation files are not visible.
Requires Bun and a valid Linear API key with access to the target workspace.
Read-only documentation does not create, update, or comment on issues.
Returned data depends on Linear API permissions and workspace configuration.

use_cases.title: Sprint Triage
use_cases.description: List issues by team, status, and limit before a planning meeting.

use_cases.title: Support Handoff
use_cases.description: Fetch a specific issue by key to confirm current status and owner.

use_cases.title: Project Review
use_cases.description: Filter issues by project to inspect active work without switching tools.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Linear issues read skill to list the first 10 issues for the Engineering team.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to get issue ENG-123 and show the command output without extra formatting.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use JSON output for Mount Vernon project issues, then summarize blockers after I confirm the command result.

output_examples.output: A terminal table shows issue keys, titles, statuses, assignees, and project details when available.
The issue details are printed in the terminal, including title, status, assignee, and related metadata.

output_examples.input: Filter project issues and request structured output.
output_examples.output: Structured issue data appears in the terminal for downstream tools or user requested analysis.

best_practices: Use a least-privilege Linear API key and rotate it regularly.
Confirm filters before running commands against large workspaces.
Ask for analysis only after the raw command output is visible.
anti_patterns: Do not store LINEAR_API_KEY in committed files.
Do not run the commands before verifying the packaged implementation.
Do not use this skill for write operations or issue updates.

faq.question: Does this skill modify Linear issues?
faq.answer: No. The documented commands are read-only and focus on listing or viewing issues.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: It requires LINEAR_API_KEY from the environment or a project .env file.

faq.question: Which runtime is required?
faq.answer: The instructions require Bun to run the Linear CLI commands.

faq.question: Can it filter issues?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented list command supports team, project, assignee, status, limit, and JSON output options.

faq.question: Can it return structured output?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands include a structured output option for tool processing.

faq.question: Are implementation files included?
faq.answer: No implementation files are present in the scanned package. Verify the installed package includes the referenced scripts before use.
